key_insight: A multi-protein serum/CSF signature, not a single marker, better stratifies survival and disease progression in ALS.
clinical_relevance: These circulating proteins could help improve prognostic enrichment, trial stratification, and future individualized risk assessment in ALS.
method: Longitudinal high-depth proximity extension assay proteomics on 1,095 serum and CSF samples from 426 people with ALS
Age- and sex-adjusted Cox regression to find proteins associated with survival
Penalised Cox and joint modeling to build and validate a prognostic protein panel, with orthogonal replication in an external cohort
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 1,095 samples from 426 ALS patients and externally replicated findings in 349 additional ALS patients, identifying 57 serum and 5 CSF survival-associated proteins.
watch_item: The biomarker panel needs further prospective validation and standardization before it can be used routinely in clinical settings.
paper_title: Circulating protein profiling identifies prognostic biomarkers in amyotrophic lateral Sclerosis
